SEBI Extends IPO Size-Adjustment Relief Until 2027

India’s securities regulator SEBI has extended the temporary relaxation that allows listed companies to revise the fresh issue size of an initial public offering by up to 50 percent without filing a new draft prospectus, with the extension running until March 2027. The rule, first introduced in April, also removes the need for additional regulatory compliance when the issue size is increased or decreased. SEBI noted that nearly ₹1 lakh crore was raised through IPOs in the July‑September quarter, underscoring the market impact of the relief.
